mainTopic: Finishing the derivation that תרומת מעשר works like תרומה גדולה, then a new משנה about produce or money set aside for separating תרומות ומעשרות, and when we must worry that it was lost
overview: The amud opens by finishing a source: the פסוק speaks of two kinds of תרומה, so the rules of תרומה גדולה also apply to תרומת מעשר. Both can be taken by estimate and by thought, and the בעל הבית may separate both. Then a new משנה begins. Someone who sets aside produce for separating תרומות ומעשרות, or money for redeeming מעשר שני, may later separate with them on the presumption that they still exist. If they turn out to be lost, רבי אלעזר says he must worry 'מעת לעת'. רבי יהודה adds that wine set aside this way must be checked at three set seasons of the year. The גמרא asks what 'מעת לעת' means, and רבי יוחנן says it means counting back 24 hours from the check that found the items missing. A second explanation, in the name of רבי אלעזר ברבי ינאי, begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two kinds of תרומה are compared: both can be taken by estimate and by thought
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק refers to two תרומות, תרומה גדולה and תרומת מעשר, so they share the same rules. Just as תרומה גדולה can be taken by estimate and by thought, so can תרומת מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse is talking about two kinds of תרומה: one is תרומה גדולה and the other is תרומת מעשר. Just as תרומה גדולה can be taken by estimating the amount and even just by thinking it, so too תרומת מעשר can be taken by estimating and by thought.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a source that reads one פסוק as covering two types of תרומה, so that the rules of one carry over to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because both kinds of תרומה are mentioned together in one פסוק, the source compares them. The first rule carried over is that you don't need an exact measurement (באומד), and you don't even have to separate it physically, since a thought is enough (במחשבה).

keyTerms.meaning: The main תרומה the owner gives to the כהן from his produce
The tenth of the לוי's מעשר that is given to a כהן
By thought alone, without physically separating it

phrases.english: The verse speaks of two terumot:
phrases.notes: The פסוק is במדבר 18:27, which says 'your תרומה' and is read as including two kinds.

phrases.english: one is the great (standard) teruma
and one is teruma of the tithe.
Just as the great teruma
is taken by estimate and by thought,
so too teruma of the tithe
is taken by estimate and by thought.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a source derivation begun before this part of the daf
steps.raayaObject: That תרומת מעשר shares the rules of תרומה גדולה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A פסוק that mentions both kinds of תרומה together

steps.title: The homeowner may separate תרומת מעשר too
steps.stepSummary: The same comparison teaches that just as the בעל הבית may separate תרומה גדולה, he may also separate תרומת מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And just as the homeowner has the right to separate תרומה גדולה, so too the homeowner has the right to separate תרומת מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The source finishes with a second rule that comes from the same comparison: the homeowner himself may separate תרומת מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought only the לוי, who receives the מעשר, can separate תרומת מעשר from it. The comparison to תרומה גדולה shows that the בעל הבית may do it too.

keyTerms.meaning: Permission, the right to do something
The homeowner, the owner of the produce

steps.whatToRemember: תרומת מעשר follows the rules of תרומה גדולה: it can be taken by estimate and by thought, and the homeowner may separate it.

phrases.english: And just as there is permission
for the homeowner to separate the great teruma,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ יֵשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְבַעַל הַבַּיִת
phrases.english: so too the homeowner has permission
to separate teruma of the tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְבַעַל הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second rule from the same comparison
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The בעל הבית may separate תרומת מעשר just as he separates תרומה גדולה.

steps.title: Produce or money set aside for later separations is presumed to still exist
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that someone who set aside produce for תרומות ומעשרות, or money for redeeming מעשר שני, may later separate with them, assuming they are still there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who puts aside produce so he can later use it to separate תרומה and מעשרות, or puts aside money so he can later redeem מעשר שני onto it, may separate with them on the presumption that they still exist.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says you may rely on the חזקה that the produce or coins you set aside are still around when you use them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he later declares that the separation should take effect on the stored produce or coins, he isn't looking at them. The משנה says he doesn't have to worry that they got lost in the meantime, because the default assumption is that they still exist.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sets aside or puts away
Second tithe, which may be redeemed onto money
On the presumption that they still exist

steps.whyThisMatters: This fits מסכת גיטין's theme of relying on a חזקה that something still exists, like presuming the husband is alive when the גט is delivered.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who sets aside produce,
in order to separate with them teruma and tithes;

phrases.aramaic: מָעוֹת, לִהְיוֹת מַפְרִישׁ עֲלֵיהֶן מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי –
phrases.english: or money, in order to separate second tithe with it,
phrases.notes: He means redeeming מעשר שני by moving its holiness onto these coins.

phrases.english: may separate with them on the presumption that they still exist.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּנִּיחַ פֵּירוֹת, לִהְיוֹת מַפְרִישׁ עֲלֵיהֶן תְּרוּמָה וּמַעַשְׂרוֹת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may separate using produce or money set aside earlier, presuming they still exist.

steps.title: If they were lost, he must worry 'from time to time'
steps.stepSummary: If the set-aside produce or money turns out to be lost, רבי אלעזר says he must be concerned 'מעת לעת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they were lost, he must be concerned from time to time. These are the words of רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה limits the presumption: once he finds the items missing, he must worry that recent separations didn't work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The presumption that the items exist stops working once we know they are gone. רבי אלעזר does not make him worry about every separation back to when he first set them aside, only about a limited window called 'מעת לעת', which the גמרא will define.

keyTerms.meaning: From a time back to the same time, a 24-hour period

steps.confusionAlert: 'מעת לעת' doesn't mean 'from time to time' in the English sense of 'sometimes'. It means a full period from one hour back to the same hour.

phrases.english: If they were lost, he must be concerned
from time to time; these are the words of Rabbi Elazar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אָבְדוּ הֲרֵי זֶה חוֹשֵׁשׁ מֵעֵת לְעֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the presumption of step 3 once a loss is found
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the items are found lost, he must worry about separations made within the previous 'מעת לעת'.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: wine set aside is checked three times a year
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says wine set aside for separating is checked at three set seasons: the east wind after סוכות, when the grape buds appear, and when water fills the unripe grapes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: one checks the wine at three times: when the east wind blows after the חג, when the grape buds come out, and when water enters the unripe grapes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a rule about wine set aside for separating: it must be checked at three points in the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine can turn into vinegar, and then it can't be used to separate for regular wine. Since these three seasons bring changes that can spoil wine, he requires a check at each one instead of relying forever on the presumption that the wine is still good.

keyTerms.meaning: Young grape buds just after the blossom

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה presumes set-aside items still exist. רבי אלעזר limits the worry after a loss to 'מעת לעת', and רבי יהודה requires checking wine at three seasons.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
At three times one checks the wine:
phrases.notes: This is wine set aside for separating, checked to see whether it has turned to vinegar.

phrases.english: when the east wind blows at the end of the festival,
and when the grape buds come out,
and at the time water enters the unripe grapes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה פְּרָקִים בּוֹדְקִין אֶת הַיַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second opinion and rule about checking stored wine
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine set aside for separating must be checked at three set seasons of the year.

steps.title: What does 'מעת לעת' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the meaning of רבי אלעזר's phrase 'מעת לעת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'from time to time' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by asking what exact time period 'מעת לעת' refers to. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה didn't say where the 24-hour period starts counting from. The question asks for that starting point so we know which separations must be redone.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is meant by 'from time to time'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a phrase in step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where the 'מעת לעת' period begins and ends

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: count back 24 hours from the check
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the period runs from the time he checked and found the items missing, back to the same hour the day before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: it means from the time of the checking back to the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the first answer: the 24 hours are counted from the moment he checked and found the items gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any separation he relied on during the 24 hours before discovering the loss must be redone. Separations made earlier than that are still trusted, based on the original presumption.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
From the time of the checking back to the same time.
phrases.notes: Count back a full day from the moment he checked and found the items missing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר מֵעֵת לְעֵת שֶׁל בְּדִיקָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The period is the 24 hours before the check that found the items lost.

steps.title: A second explanation is introduced in the name of רבי אלעזר ברבי ינאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן אנטיגנוס begins to give another explanation of 'מעת לעת', quoting רבי אלעזר ברבי ינאי. His words continue on the next part of the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן אנטיגנוס says in the name of רבי אלעזר son of רבי ינאי:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is introducing a second answer to the question. Only the names appear here, and the actual explanation comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing a second named authority tells us there is another way to define the period, different from רבי יוחנן's. The learner should expect a different starting point for counting the 24 hours.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Antigonus says
in the name of Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Yannai:

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a second answer to the question of step 6, alongside רבי יוחנן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not yet stated here. The explanation continues on the next part of the daf.
